subChunks.title: State Management: Zustand
subChunks.hookHtml: Context + useReducer can handle app-wide state, but they require boilerplate and have performance limitations. Zustand is a minimal, ergonomic state management library — a global store you read from anywhere, write to from anywhere, with React re-renders scoped precisely to the data that changed. It's become the pragmatic choice for production React apps that outgrow local state.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Creating a store

import { create } from 'zustand';

const useQuestStore = create((set) => ({
  // State:
  quests: [],
  activeQuestId: null,

  // Actions:
  addQuest: (quest) => set((state) => ({
    quests: [...state.quests, quest],
  })),

  completeQuest: (id) => set((state) => ({
    quests: state.quests.map(q =>
      q.id === id ? { ...q, completed: true } : q
    ),
  })),

  setActiveQuest: (id) => set({ activeQuestId: id }),
}));

Reading from the store — selectors

// Select only what you need — component only re-renders if that slice changes:
function QuestCount() {
  const questCount = useQuestStore((state) => state.quests.length);
  return <p>{questCount} quests</p>;
}

// Multiple values:
function QuestPanel() {
  const quests = useQuestStore((state) => state.quests);
  const addQuest = useQuestStore((state) => state.addQuest);
}

Zustand vs Context

// Context: all consumers re-render when any part of the context changes.
// Fine for rarely-changing data (theme, user).

// Zustand: components subscribe to slices — only re-render for their slice.
// Better for state that changes frequently or has many consumers.

Persisting state

import { create } from 'zustand';
import { persist } from 'zustand/middleware';

const useSettingsStore = create(
  persist(
    (set) => ({
      theme: 'light',
      setTheme: (theme) => set({ theme }),
    }),
    { name: 'settings-storage' } // localStorage key
  )
);

When to reach for Zustand

Vex: "The honest progression: start with useState (local). When siblings need to share, lift to parent. When the chain gets long, try component composition. When you need truly global state that many components read from — authentication, cart, notification queue — Zustand. It's not about scale, it's about the right tool for the shape of the problem."

Immer integration for complex updates

import { create } from 'zustand';
import { immer } from 'zustand/middleware/immer';

const useStore = create(immer((set) => ({
  quests: [],
  completeQuest: (id) => set((state) => {
    // Write mutating code — immer handles immutability:
    const quest = state.quests.find(q => q.id === id);
    if (quest) quest.completed = true;
  }),
})));

storyBeats.text: The academy's quest board needs to be visible from the header, the sidebar, and three different page components. Prop drilling is twelve levels deep. Vex opens a new file.

storyBeats.speaker: Vex the Interface Weaver
storyBeats.text: Context solves prop drilling, but every consumer re-renders when any part of the context changes. Zustand solves both problems: global state accessible from anywhere, with re-renders scoped to exactly the slice each component subscribed to. The store lives outside React's tree.

storyBeats.speaker: Vex the Interface Weaver
storyBeats.text: Create a store with create(). Define state and actions together. Subscribe in components with a selector that picks only what you need. The component re-renders only when its selected slice changes — nothing else.

storyBeats.speaker: Zustand store — define and consume

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a cart system using Zustand:

  • Create a useCartStore with: items: [], addItem(item), removeItem(id)
  • Build a <ProductCard name price id /> that shows whether the product is in the cart and has an Add/Remove button with appropriate data-testid
  • Build a <CartCount /> that subscribes to only items.length — it should show count data-testid="cart-count"

guidedPracticeTests.label: Clicking Add increases cart count to 1

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a notification system using Zustand from scratch. The store holds notifications: [] (each with id, message, type: 'success' | 'error'). Actions: addNotification(message, type) and dismissNotification(id). Build a <NotificationBell /> that shows the unread count, and a <NotificationList /> that renders all notifications with dismiss buttons. Persist notifications to localStorage using Zustand's persist middleware.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Compare Zustand with React Context for global state management. When would you choose each? Explain what Zustand's selector pattern does for performance that Context cannot do natively. Then explain the function form of set() vs the object form — why does the distinction matter?

questions.prompt: In Zustand, a component uses the selector `state => state.items.length`. When will it re-render?
options: Only when the items array length changes — not when item details change
Whenever any part of the store changes
Only when the component explicitly calls a store action
On every parent re-render, like normal props
questions.answer: Only when the items array length changes — not when item details change
questions.explanation: Zustand runs the selector after every store update and compares the result with the previous result. If the result is the same (items.length hasn't changed), the component doesn't re-render. A component that only selects the count won't re-render when an item's name or price changes — only when items are added or removed.

questions.prompt: In a Zustand action, why use `set(state => ({ ... }))` (function form) rather than `set({ ... })` (object form)?
options: The function form guarantees you're reading the latest state — the object form can be stale if multiple updates are queued
The object form overwrites the entire store; the function form only updates specified keys
The function form supports async actions; the object form does not
They are identical — the function form is just more verbose
questions.answer: The function form guarantees you're reading the latest state — the object form can be stale if multiple updates are queued
questions.explanation: set({ quests: [...state.quests, newQuest] }) captures state from the outer closure, which might be stale if multiple actions are dispatched before React processes them. set(prev => ({ quests: [...prev.quests, newQuest] })) receives the latest committed state from Zustand's update queue. For most single actions this doesn't matter, but it's a good habit for actions that depend on previous state.

options: Automatically serialises the store to localStorage (or another storage) and rehydrates it on page load
Prevents the store from being garbage collected when no components are subscribed
Persists actions to a Redux DevTools log for debugging
Caches the store's computed selectors between renders
questions.answer: Automatically serialises the store to localStorage (or another storage) and rehydrates it on page load
questions.explanation: persist wraps your store and, on every state update, serialises it to the specified storage (localStorage by default). On app load, if stored data exists under the store's name key, it rehydrates the store with that data. This gives you persistent state (cart contents, user preferences) with a single middleware addition.

questions.prompt: You need to share the authenticated user object across 30+ components. Zustand or Context — which is more appropriate, and why?
options: Either works well here — the user object rarely changes (only on login/logout), so Context's 'all consumers re-render' behaviour has minimal impact
Zustand — it always outperforms Context for any shared state
Context — Zustand is only appropriate for local component state
Neither — use a global variable and trigger re-renders manually
questions.answer: Either works well here — the user object rarely changes (only on login/logout), so Context's 'all consumers re-render' behaviour has minimal impact
questions.explanation: Context's performance limitation only matters when the shared state changes frequently. The authenticated user changes once on login and once on logout. With 30 components re-rendering twice per session, Context is perfectly fine. Zustand is a better choice when the state changes frequently (a cart, notification queue, or real-time data) and many components are subscribed.
